name: WysLeap Analytics
author: wysleap

sections.description:
WysLeap Analytics adds the WysLeap tracking script to every page of your site. Paste your site ID and API key, and visits start showing up in your WysLeap dashboard.

This plugin needs a WysLeap account. Sign up at wysleap.com, add your site’s domain, and copy the site ID and API key from your site’s Settings. The plugin is free; WysLeap is a paid service that starts with a 30-day free trial, no credit card.

What you see in WysLeap

  • Analytics with bots taken out: known bots, headless and automated browsers are flagged and kept out of your human numbers, with raw and clean views side by side.
  • Session replay and click and scroll heatmaps, so you can watch where visitors get stuck.
  • A buying-intent score for every visitor, and a list of your highest-intent visitors.
  • WysAI themes: what changed on your site, the likely cause, the evidence from your own data and a suggested fix.
  • No cookies: each visitor gets a random ID in browser storage, and no names or emails are collected.

What you can turn on

  • Page views (always on)
  • Clicks
  • Scroll depth
  • Session replay, with form fields and sensitive text masked

What the plugin handles for you

  • Leaves out your own visits: logged-in administrators and editors aren’t tracked by default (pick any roles).
  • Skips admin pages, previews, the Customizer and feeds.
  • Optional consent mode: works with cookie banners that support the WP Consent API. Tracking starts only after the visitor allows “statistics”, and withdrawing consent opts them out.
  • Adds suggested text to your privacy policy (Settings → Privacy).

For developers

  • wysleap_analytics_should_track filter: return false to skip tracking on a page.
  • wysleap_analytics_init_config filter: change the config passed to WysLeap.init().

External services

This plugin connects your site to WysLeap, an analytics service run by WysLeap (wysleap.com). It does nothing until you enter a site ID and API key.

Once set up, every tracked page loads the script https://wysleap.com/telemetry.js in the visitor’s browser. That script sends WysLeap the page address and referrer, browser and device details, the visitor’s approximate location from their IP address, and, if you turn them on, clicks, scroll depth and a session replay with form fields and sensitive text masked. It stores a random visitor ID in the browser and may recognise the device across visits. Visitors in the EU/EEA, UK and Switzerland are only recognised that way after giving consent.

  • Terms of service: https://wysleap.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://wysleap.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin from Plugins → Add New.
  2. Go to Settings → WysLeap Analytics.
  3. Paste your site ID and API key from your WysLeap dashboard and save.
  4. Visit your site in a private window, then check your WysLeap dashboard.
sections.faq:
Do I need a WysLeap account?

Yes. The plugin only adds the script; your reports live in the WysLeap dashboard at wysleap.com.

Why don’t I see my own visits?

Logged-in administrators and editors are not tracked by default. Change this under “Don’t track”, or test in a private window.

Is the API key secret?

No. It is meant for the browser and appears in your page source, as with any analytics snippet. Your dashboard is protected by your WysLeap login.

I already pasted the WysLeap snippet into my theme.

Remove it from your theme (or header/footer plugin) before activating this plugin, so pages aren’t counted twice.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The script runs in the visitor’s browser, so cached pages are tracked normally.

Does it track WooCommerce orders?

Not automatically. It tracks your store’s pages, but orders aren’t sent. To see revenue, add a WysLeap purchase event to your order confirmation page: https://wysleap.com/docs/purchases

Does it show AI crawlers like GPTBot or ClaudeBot?

Only the ones that run JavaScript, and most don’t. The plugin adds a browser script, so it can’t see requests that never load it. To count every AI crawler visit, report them to WysLeap from your server or CDN: https://wysleap.com/docs/ai-crawlers
